/no_think
You are the scope check for MedX, an assistant for psychiatry and mental health based on the DSM-5.

In scope: mental disorders (diagnosis, criteria, symptoms, course, prevalence, risk factors, differential
diagnosis), psychiatric treatment and psychopharmacology, substance use, intoxication and withdrawal, sleep,
eating, neurocognitive and neurodevelopmental disorders, personality, psychotherapy, suicide and self-harm,
and behavioral science.

Out of scope: questions mainly about another field of medicine (cardiology, pulmonology, infectious disease,
biochemistry, endocrinology, surgery, otology and so on), even when the patient also mentions stress, mood,
anxiety or sleep in passing. Judge what the question is asking, not incidental details of the case.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"in_scope": true or false, "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
Question:
A 40-year-old man is brought into the emergency department by his wife complaining of intense lower right abdominal pain. An abdominal CT scan was performed which noted a dilated appendix with a thickened wall and the accumulation of extraluminal fluid. A quick history is taken while the OR is prepped for surgery. Past medical history is noncontributory and the patient takes no medications. Social history reveals a sedentary lifestyle. The patient admits to regularly drinking several beers and several shots of vodka every night. He had to stop drinking 2 days ago due to the intense abdominal pain. The patient is brought into the OR and the inflamed and necrotic appendix is removed. He is admitted to the hospital for overnight monitoring. Later that night, the patient begins to hallucinate. Which type of hallucination is this patient likely to experience?

Options:
A. Proprioceptive hallucinations
B. Olfactory hallucination
C. Gustatory hallucination
D. Hypnagogic hallucination
E. Tactile hallucination

text: {"in_scope": true, "reason": "The question concerns hallucinations occurring during alcohol withdrawal, which falls under substance use and psychiatric symptoms."}
